plan.estimand: Minimum development sample size for internal validation of a survival prediction model meeting Riley et al. precision criteria
plan.hypothesis: The fitted Cox model with 30 candidate predictors achieves acceptable prediction accuracy after internal validation shrinkage, meeting precision criteria for both model calibration and apparent–adjusted R² overfitting margin
assumptions: Proportional hazards assumption holds for the Cox model
Internal validation (e.g. cross-validation or bootstrapping) will apply shrinkage factor 0.90 to predictions
Precision criteria centre on Nagelkerke R² scale for overfitting margin (apparent – adjusted difference ≤ 0.05)
Overall event rate 0.065 per person-year is stable across the development cohort
Prediction horizon and mean follow-up define the observation window
Default pmsampsize criteria applied (number of uncorrected candidate predictors, EPV rules, and overfitting margin)
missing_information: Clarification on whether the 'adjusted Cox-Snell R²' of 0.051 refers to: (a) the expected or planned adjusted R² after internal validation shrinkage, (b) the initial unadjusted R² from model fitting, or (c) a pre-specified target for the full model
Confirmation of the internal validation method (bootstrap, cross-fold, other) that will implement the 0.90 shrinkage
Specification of any additional pmsampsize options (e.g. fine-tuning of EPV multiple, non-linear penalty scaling) beyond the 'default' package criteria
clarification_questions: Does the adjusted Cox-Snell R² = 0.051 represent the expected performance *after* internal shrinkage (i.e. the target adjusted R²), or is this the initial model performance before shrinkage?

Confirm: the 95% confidence level and 0.05 maximum overfitting margin (Nagelkerke scale) are the only precision constraints, or are there additional clinical or operational thresholds (e.g. calibration slope, discrimination)?

For verification of the 0.05 absolute margin of error on predicted outcome risk at prediction horizon 2 years: should this be computed as a confidence interval half-width around the Kaplan–Meier or model-predicted 2-year survival probability?
scientific_notes: Riley et al. (2018, 2020) provide sample-size methodology for prediction model development, balancing overfitting penalty (via events-per-variable, shrinkage) and precision of key performance measures on the Nagelkerke scale.

pmsampsize 1.1.3 (Archer et al., R package) implements Riley criteria for continuous, binary and survival endpoints. For survival, the method uses Cox partial likelihood and accounts for censoring via event rate and follow-up duration.

The combination of 30 candidate predictors, low R² (0.051), and moderate event rate (0.065/year over 2.07 years mean follow-up ≈ 13–14% overall event rate) suggests a sparse signal; pmsampsize will likely recommend a substantial sample to separate overfitting margin and achieve the 0.05 margin of error on risk.
Numerical execution is required to obtain the exact recommended sample size, verify shrinkage and achieved precision metrics.
